text:
acme_ops: Hi — since ~10:30 PST we're seeing intermittent 503s and some requests with 8-12s latency. Our app logs don't have any request IDs. Can you tell us what to pull so you can debug?

jess: Sorry you're hitting this. The fastest things we need are: 1) one raw HTTP request (headers + body) that hit the error, 2) a timestamp, and 3) any SDK logs around the request. If you can get a HAR or a curl that'd be ideal.

acme_ops: We mainly have server logs (Node). No x-request-id in them. Using node SDK 0.7.2. How do we surface the id?

maria: Quick tip — Node SDK injects an outbound header named `x-rd-request-id` (it can also appear as `X-Request-Id` depending on your proxy). If you set the debug env var the SDK will print correlation ids: `RD_SDK_DEBUG=1 node app.js` — look for lines like `rd_request_id=abcd1234`.

samir: If you prefer a single step you can reproduce locally with curl. Minimal replay (remove keys before posting here):

````
curl -v 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_WITH_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -H "X-Rd-Request-Id: YOUR_OBSERVED_ID" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-like","input":"hello"}' 
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
````

samir: When you run that with `-v` we'll see the response headers and the server request id. If the header above isn't present in your logs, omit `-H "X-Rd-Request-Id"` so the server assigns one.

jess: If you can't share a curl, a HAR file is excellent. Chrome steps: Network tab -> reproduce -> right click -> Save all as HAR with content. Then attach the HAR. In the saved HAR open the POST to `/v1/generate` and copy the `request.headers` block — that contains the correlation header, user agent and any proxies.

acme_ops: Mobile SDK question — how do I get the id from iOS logs?

maria: For mobile: enable verbose logs in the SDK: iOS: set `RDLogLevel = .debug` in config; Android: `Redwood.enableDebugLogging(true)`. Then reproduce and look at device logs: Android `adb logcat | grep rd_request`, iOS run Console.app and search `rd_request_id` or `redwood`. The SDK will print something like `rd_request_id=abcd1234 span=...`.

jess: Another useful artifact is the Console debug token. From Redwood Console: go to Requests -> filter by time -> click the request -> Copy Debug Token (button). That token lets us pull the server-side trace without needing the full HAR. If you share the debug token, do NOT include your API key. Debug tokens look like `rd-debug-abc123` (example).

samir: For escalations to eng-oncall include: environment, timestamp (UTC), route (e.g., `/v1/generate`), request id/debug token, sample payload (trim PII), and either HAR or curl output. If the customer can provide both client-side and server-side timestamps that's really helpful to correlate spans.

acme_ops: Got it — attaching a small HAR and a curl output in a DM now. Also sending timestamp: 2026-03-17T18:42:11Z.

jess: Perfect. I copied the debug token from the HAR entry (rd-debug-xyz789) and added it to the ticket. Please redact/remove Authorization headers before attaching.

samir: Thanks — I'll pull the trace using that debug token and post updates here. If I need the full debug bundle I'll ask; otherwise this should be enough to see where the 503 or long tail is coming from.

deploy-bot: Incident note created: #INC-2026-142 — assigned to samir.

jess: Closing loop for now — if you see more requests please paste any new `x-rd-request-id` values here or attach another HAR. :thumbsup:
